About this document


This document provides the teaching content for Economics Years 12–13 of the
New Zealand Curriculum. Equivalent for Te Marautanga o Aotearoa is being
published separately.

Progress and assessment information for Economics Years 12–13 is still in
development. Once that is completed, Economics Years 12–13 is proposed to be
made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum Statement under section
90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Economics Years 12–13 will be required to start using it in Year 12 from
1 January 2029, and in Year 13 from 1 January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.

 Students are taught about how economic decisions and events shape societies.
 Students are taught key economic concepts such as the roles of consumers and
 businesses, and how scarcity and choice shape market forces and affect
 economic outcomes. Students are taught to apply economic concepts, models,
 and values to explain how consumers, businesses, governments, and
 communities interact and make informed decisions.

Students are taught core economic concepts, models, theories, and frameworks that
explain how individuals, businesses, governments, and societies make decisions
about the allocation of scarce resources. Students explain how economic systems,
market mechanisms, and economic activity influence outcomes in local, national, and
global contexts.

Economics provides students with the knowledge and practices to examine economic
issues, data, models, and policies in real-world and theoretical contexts. This
disciplinary knowledge helps students develop expertise in applying economic
concepts, frameworks, and evidence to analyse economic behaviour, interpret
patterns and relationships, and explain how economic decisions affect markets,
communities, and economies.

As students progress through Year 12–13, they are taught to analyse, evaluate, and
synthesise economic information and perspectives to reach reasoned conclusions
and justify decisions in written form. This enables them to communicate evidence-
based arguments and recommendations that consider economic, social, cultural,
environmental, and long-term implications across a range of economic contexts.

 Economics leads to pathways in Economics and in related areas such as
 business, finance, public policy, and global development.
